title: Gideon and the Compass
premise: In the winter of 1921, as the Republic of Vessany collapses under advancing loyalist armies, courier Ivo Kavanagh is entrusted with a coded ledger proving the government sold its own borders to a foreign power. At a safehouse in the river town of Gellbruck, a stranger leaves a child on the doorstep with one instruction: forget the face. The child, Mirei, is the daughter of the minister who wrote the ledger, and her presence makes Ivo's invisibility impossible. As Ivo and Mirei move upriver through three checkpoints, pursued by the minister's former aide who needs the ledger destroyed, Ivo learns the courier who carried it before them was Mirei's mother—and Ivo's lost love. At the third checkpoint, with the ice cracking on the river, Ivo must choose between burning the evidence to save Mirei or delivering it and letting history happen to them. They choose the child, smuggling her across the broken ice while the ledger burns, but Ivo has memorized its contents—and in the epilogue's final beat, testifies anonymously years later, choosing at last to belong to history.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed interwar states, an obsession that seeps into every page she writes. She lives near a slow, ice-bound river and insists she began writing fiction only to give the forgotten couriers of history someone to carry their letters home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the capital, Ivo receives the sealed ledger and final instructions as the government evacuates around them. Ivo, a courier who prides himself on being unnoticed, treats the mission as routine. Emotional beat: the quiet arrogance of believing you are a bystander to history.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, at the Gellbruck safehouse. A knock at night; a girl of seven, Mirei, frozen and silent, with a note: forget the face. Ivo wants to hand her to the town constable but cannot. Emotional beat: the first crack in Ivo's practiced indifference.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deciphering part of the ledger, Ivo recognizes the minister's cipher hand—and a marginal note in a handwriting Ivo knows intimately: Lena's, the courier who vanished years ago. Mirei's surname confirms it. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as obligation.

chapters.title: The Aide in Grey
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the aide, Sorren, arriving in Gellbruck, charming the checkpoint officers, hunting the ledger. He is not a fanatic but a pragmatist who believes burning the truth saves lives. Emotional beat: the reader meets a villain who is almost right.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One River
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo maps the route upriver: the mill checkpoint, the bridge, the ferry at the ice. Mirei, sharp and watchful, proves useful, memorizing faces. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into something like family.

chapters.title: The Mill
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. First checkpoint: Ivo bluffs through as a grain merchant, but a soldier notices Mirei's fine boots. They escape through the millrace, and Ivo is wounded. Emotional beat: invisibility is over; they are now fugitives with a name.

chapters.title: What Lena Left
chapters.summary: Mirei's POV, her first narration. She reveals she remembers her mother hiding the ledger copy and whispering a name: Ivo. She has been carrying a compass her mother gave her, which points not north but toward a hidden dead-drop. Emotional beat: the child has been the mission's true keeper all along.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Gellbruck
chapters.summary: Sorren corners Ivo at the second checkpoint and offers a trade: the ledger for safe passage for the girl. Ivo nearly accepts. Mirei, listening, runs. Emotional beat: duty and love pull in opposite directions, and Ivo hesitates too long.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Climax at the ferry checkpoint as the river ice cracks. Sorren takes the ledger; Ivo lets it go, then reveals the contents are memorized. In the chaos of the breaking ice, Ivo and Mirei cross on the shifting floes, Sorren drowning in his certainty—or choosing the river. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the discovery that some evidence lives in a person, not a paper.

chapters.title: Forget the Face
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with a coda years later. Ivo and Mirei reach safety across the border, anonymous in a refugee column. Years on, Ivo testifies under seal, finally choosing to be part of history rather than its courier. Emotional beat: belonging is not being remembered—it is choosing to matter.
